title: Danawa operator Connectwave confirms external intrusion and a partial leak of member information, ZDNet Korea reports
date_note: Boannews (26 November) says service was halted on 26 November; the page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: country; the article gives no city
summary: ZDNet Korea reports that Connectwave, which runs the Danawa price-comparison platform, says in an apology that it confirmed a security incident caused by unauthorized external access. Its investigation confirmed that some member information leaked: name, ID, mobile phone number and phone number. The company says passwords and payment information were not leaked. The scale, the route and the attack type were not given, and service had not resumed.
plain: Danawa, a Korean price-comparison site, says outsiders got in and some member details leaked: names, IDs and phone numbers. The company says passwords and payment details were not leaked.
exec: Connectwave says some Danawa member information leaked after an external intrusion; it has not given the scale or a date for service to resume.
action: Connectwave says it will notify promptly if further leaks are confirmed; watch for its notice.
impact: Some member information (name, ID, phone numbers) leaked, per Connectwave; service not yet resumed.

sources.name: Boannews: 가격 비교 플랫폼 ‘다나와’ 해킹 추정 사고... 서비스 일시 중단
ZDNet Korea: 다나와 회원정보 일부 유출 확인

validation.note: Boannews (Connectwave notice of suspected intrusion) and ZDNet Korea (Connectwave apology confirming intrusion and partial leak); neither Connectwave page was read, so the core leak fact rests on ZDNet Korea only.

review.note: stronger than the source: reported to the authorities now carrying out the reporting process; security incident now suspected external intrusion per Boannews
